question: Votes with Trump?
headline: TBD
rule: Counts every House roll call on final disposition of a measure (passage, adopting a resolution, concurring in a Senate amendment, or suspending the rules and passing it) for which the White House issued a statement of administration policy that states a position on passage. Support means Trump wanted a Yea; opposition means a Nay. The rule applies to every member of either party; the votes that were examined but not counted, and why, are listed below.
why: Proposed headline thresholds, not yet approved: "Reliably with Trump" at 95% or more of counted votes cast with his position and with it on every vote where 10 or more of the member's own party voted the other way; "Mostly with Trump" at 80% to 94%; "Often against Trump" below 80%. The headline stays "Coming soon" until these are approved.
summary: Cast the White House position on 113 of 113 counted votes and the opposite on 0. The headline stays Coming soon until the rule is approved.

section.title: House Republican leadership and Trump
section.note: Contributions from each leader's campaign committee, leadership PAC and joint fundraising committees, from the NRCC, and from President Trump's committees, from FEC filings. Committees are matched by FEC committee ID. Roles are from house.gov and the Clerk. Super PACs such as the Congressional Leadership Fund cannot give to candidates; their independent spending is not counted here. For Mike Johnson himself, transfers from his own joint fundraising committee (the Johnson Leadership Fund) are not listed as leader gifts, since the committee is his own.

mandate.intro: Heritage Foundation's Mandate for Leadership (2023) is the Project 2025 policy book. Each row quotes a Mandate proposal with its page, then the bill or vote it matches. “Direct” means the Mandate names the bill or the same action; “same target” means the bill acts on the same subject in the Mandate's direction; “partial” says exactly where the bill differs. A match shows alignment of policy, not intent or coordination.

method.text: This is not an exhaustive review. The Mandate has no index of bills, so the matches come from searching its text for subjects that bills in this Congress address. 130 measures had a White House statement (the set on the Trump section above). The 11 subjects below were searched; 7 had a Mandate proposal that the measures voted on follow, listed in the table, covering 9 measures and 10 votes. 3 were read and rejected and 1 had no Mandate text. The other measures were not individually checked against the Mandate, so more matches may exist. Two matches are marked partial and say exactly how the bill differs from the Mandate. Mandate matches apply to Republican members only; they are one signal among several, not a symmetrical measure like the Trump votes.

rows.proposal: Enact the Midnight Rules Relief Act, so several late-term regulations can be disapproved together
rows.quote: Congress and the President should enact the Midnight Rules Relief Act
rows.match: The Mandate names this bill. H.R. 77 provides for en bloc consideration of resolutions disapproving “midnight rules.”

rows.proposal: Prevent a central bank digital currency
rows.quote: Prevent the institution of a central bank digital currency (CBDC).
rows.match: H.R. 1919 prohibits the use of a central bank digital currency for monetary policy and bars Federal Reserve banks from offering certain products directly to individuals.

rows.proposal: Limit California's Clean Air Act waiver
rows.quote: Restore the position that California’s waiver applies only to California-specific issues like ground-level ozone, not global climate issues.
rows.match: The Mandate calls for narrowing California's waiver. H.J.Res. 87 uses the Congressional Review Act to nullify EPA's waiver decision on Advanced Clean Trucks and related rules.

rows.quote: Congress should eliminate ambiguous discretionary language in Title 8 that aliens “may” be detained and clarify that aliens “shall” be detained.
rows.match: Same mechanism, narrower scope: S. 5 requires detention of certain aliens charged with or arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, shoplifting or assault of a law enforcement officer.

rows.proposal: Enforce and strengthen Section 117 reporting of foreign gifts to universities
rows.quote: Reverse the Biden Administration’s refusal to enforce Section 117 of the HEA
rows.match: Same provision, different remedy: H.R. 1048 rewrites Section 117 with a $50,000 reporting threshold and fines. The Mandate's further proposal, tying reporting to federal aid, is not in the bill.
